1: Chapter 1: A Visitor on a Rainy Night

It had been raining in Qingshi for three days straight. Lin Xiaoyu shut the door of the pharmacy and lit the last lamp. She was twenty-two, and after her father passed away, she had kept the little pharmacy running all on her own.
"Is anyone there?" a man's voice called from outside.

Lin Xiaoyu hesitated, then opened the door. A young man stood in the doorway, soaked to the bone, his left hand pressed against his right arm, blood seeping through his fingers. He said his name was Chen Ziming, and that he had come from the provincial capital.
"I need someone to bandage me up," Chen Ziming said quietly. "I can pay. Would 120 yuan be enough?"

She didn't take his money. She just had him sit by the counter and turned to fetch gauze and medicinal wine. The wound wasn't deep, but it was long, as if sliced open by a knife. As she cleaned the wound, she asked how he had been hurt.

Chen Ziming was silent for a long while before he said, "I ran into some men on the road. They wanted a letter I was carrying." He pulled an oil-paper packet from his coat and set it on the table. "This letter has to reach Baiyun Temple before May 18."

Lin Xiaoyu glanced out the window. Baiyun Temple was up in the mountains, forty li from Qingshi, and mountain roads were at their worst in the rain. She remembered what her father always used to say: if you save someone, see it through to the end.
"I'll take you up the mountain first thing tomorrow morning," she said. "You can sleep in the back room tonight."
2: Before dawn, Lin Xiaoyu woke Chen Ziming. She had a bamboo basket on her back, packed with dry rations, medicinal herbs, and an old umbrella. Chen Ziming's arm had improved somewhat, but his face was still pale.
Halfway up the mountain, they ran into old Zhou Dashan, who was out gathering firewood. Zhou Dashan knew Lin Xiaoyu and asked with a smile where she was headed so early.
"Delivering medicine to Baiyun Temple," Lin Xiaoyu replied. She didn't mention the letter.
Zhou Dashan glanced at Chen Ziming and lowered his voice. "Last evening there were three strangers at the town entrance asking about a wounded young man. Be careful."

Chen Ziming's face went even paler. Lin Xiaoyu thanked the old man and led Chen Ziming off the main road onto a narrow path that only herb gatherers knew. The path was narrow and slippery; she walked ahead, every step sure and steady.
By noon, the rain had finally stopped. The mountain mist slowly lifted, revealing the rooftops of Baiyun Temple in the distance. A nun stood at the temple gate—Zhao Qiuyue, the temple's guest keeper.
Zhao Qiuyue took the oil-paper parcel, examined the red seal on the closure, and nodded. "My master has waited 2 years for this letter," she said. "You've had a hard journey."
On the way back, Chen Ziming said to Lin Xiaoyu, "I owe you my life." Lin Xiaoyu smiled and said, "Then the next time you come to Qingshi, you can help me fix the roof of the medicine shop."
